I found two issues: one blocking bug and one non-blocking test gap.

### 1. The proposed snapshot is the midnight before the newest security update, so that update is missed (bug, **blocks**)

- **File:** `/tmp/pr-review-eval-7c1e/runs/images83fix-p8-2/repo/renovate.json`, line 18
- **Added text:** `... & $pad($m[0], -2, "0") & "T000000Z"}]})`

The template keeps only the date from the InRelease `Date:` line and sets the time to `T000000Z`. The security pocket's `Date:` is the time it last changed, which is almost always after midnight. So the proposed snapshot is taken just before the change Renovate saw, and leaves out the fix it was meant to pick up. That fix arrives only when the pocket changes again on a later day. If no further security change comes, it never arrives. This breaks three stated guarantees:
- ADR 0019 (added line): "The Ubuntu archive snapshot bumps as soon as the archive changes, since it carries security fixes".
- The datasource `description`: "the latest is the day the security pocket last changed".
- The PR body says the same.

- **Trigger:** `http://archive.ubuntu.com/ubuntu/dists/resolute-security/InRelease` contains `Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 14:07:12 UTC`, after a security update published at that time. Nothing else is published to the pocket for the next few days.
- **Path:** `renovate.json@customDatasources.ubuntu-snapshot.transformTemplates` (regex `(\d+) (\w{3}) (\d{4})` drops the time) → release version `20261121T000000Z` → `images/core/Dockerfile@ARG UBUNTU_SNAPSHOT_VERSION` → `images/core/Dockerfile@RUN echo "APT::Snapshot ..." > /etc/apt/apt.conf.d/50snapshot` → `apt-get update --error-on=any` reads `snapshot.ubuntu.com/ubuntu/20261121T000000Z`.
- **Outcome:** The image installs the archive as it was at 00:00 on 21 Nov, without the 14:07 security fix. Every later Renovate lookup returns the same `20261121T000000Z`, so no bump is proposed. The fix stays out of all four images until another security update happens on a later day.
- **Suggested fix:** Use the time from the `Date:` line as well (also capture `(\d{2}):(\d{2}):(\d{2})` and build `YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ`). The `regex:` versioning in `images/core/Dockerfile` line 10 already accepts any `\d{6}` time. This allows more than one bump a day, so the "at most one bump a day" wording in the description and ADR 0022 would need to change. If one bump a day must stay, the code cannot both keep that and pick up the same-day fix, so the guarantee should be reworded to match what the code does.

### 2. No smoke test checks that apt actually uses the snapshot (tests, does not block)

- **File:** `/tmp/pr-review-eval-7c1e/runs/images83fix-p8-2/repo/images/core/Dockerfile`, line 14
- **Added text:** `RUN echo "APT::Snapshot \"${UBUNTU_SNAPSHOT_VERSION}\";" > /etc/apt/apt.conf.d/50snapshot \`

The main new behaviour is that apt in the image and in child images reads only the dated snapshot. Neither `images/core/smoke.sh` nor `images/smoke-lib.sh` checks this. The only evidence is the PR's manual `apt-cache policy` check. Some changes would quietly bring back floating packages and CI would stay green:
- `50snapshot` being dropped or renamed;
- a base-image sources change that turns snapshot support off;
- a child image overwriting the apt config.

**Suggested fix:** in core's smoke test, run `apt-config dump APT::Snapshot` and check the value. Optionally also check that every source listed by `apt-get indextargets` or `apt-cache policy` points at `snapshot.ubuntu.com/.../<id>`, except `download.docker.com`.

### Checked and found sound
- The manager regex `[a-z.-]+?` matches `custom.ubuntu-snapshot`, and the `versioning=regex:...$` value is captured correctly before the `ARG` line.
- `minimumReleaseAge: null` matches the existing plume-works images rule, and the `x.y.0` rule cannot match `YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ`.
- The JSONata `$match` result, `.groups` indexes, `$lookup` and `$pad` produce `YYYYMMDD` correctly when there is exactly one `Date:` line.
- The containerd.io `extractVersion` `^(?<version>[^~]+)~` and the install spec `containerd.io=${CONTAINERD_VERSION}~*` agree. The Docker deb rule now covers `containerd.io`.
- The PR body says every `apt-get update` has `--error-on=any`. That holds for all apt calls in `images/`: core has three and core-systemd has one. devcontainer-base and coder-template run no apt calls.
- `Verify-Peer=false` is limited to `snapshot.ubuntu.com` for the first `RUN` only. apt still checks the signed InRelease, so the code matches its comment.

**Dismissed findings:** none.

I found 2 issues: one blocking bug in the Renovate snapshot datasource and one non-blocking test gap.

### 1. The proposed snapshot leaves out the security fix that triggered the bump (bug, blocks)

- **File:** `/tmp/pr-review-eval-7c1e/runs/images83fix-p8-2/repo/renovate.json`, line 18
- **Added text:** `... & $pad($m[0], -2, "0") & "T000000Z"}]})`
- **Problem:** the datasource reads the date from the `Date:` line of the `resolute-security` InRelease file, which is when the pocket last changed. It then pins midnight UTC of that day. On snapshot.ubuntu.com a timestamp shows the archive as it was at that moment. That moment is before the change the `Date:` line records, so the new pin never includes the publication that caused it.
- **Stated guarantees this breaks:**
  - The `customDatasources.ubuntu-snapshot.description` ("the latest is the day the security pocket last changed").
  - The packageRule description ("it carries security fixes").
  - The PR body.
  - The fix only lands when the pocket changes again on a later day. Until then the image ships the Ubuntu package versions from before the fix, and Renovate proposes nothing because it treats the pin as current.
- **Trigger:** the security pocket is republished on 2026-11-21 at 03:12 UTC, so its InRelease reads `Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 03:12:34 UTC`. The current pin `20261121T000000Z` is exactly what this produces.
- **Path:** `renovate.json@customDatasources.ubuntu-snapshot.transformTemplates` turns the `Date:` line into `20261121T000000Z`. Then `renovate.json@customManagers[0]` rewrites `images/core/Dockerfile@ARG UBUNTU_SNAPSHOT_VERSION`. Then `images/core/Dockerfile@RUN echo "APT::Snapshot ..."` writes `/etc/apt/apt.conf.d/50snapshot`, and every `apt-get update` in core, core-systemd and CI jobs reads the archive as of 2026-11-21 00:00Z.
- **Outcome:** the security updates published at 03:12 on the 21st are missing from the images. They stay missing until the pocket changes on some later day, and even then the newest day's fixes are again left out. The PR presents the snapshot bump as a security-fix channel, so this is a wrong outcome.
- **Suggested fix:** use the full time from `Date:`, built from `$match` groups for hour, minute and second (e.g. `20261121T031234Z`). Alternatively pin the next day's midnight, which needs a date-arithmetic fallback. Either way the snapshot then includes the triggering publication. Daily bumps would no longer be limited to one per day by construction, but the `Date:` line still changes only when the pocket does.

### 2. No smoke test checks the snapshot pin that is promised to persist (tests, does not block)

- **File:** `/tmp/pr-review-eval-7c1e/runs/images83fix-p8-2/repo/images/core/Dockerfile`, line 14
- **Added text:** `RUN echo "APT::Snapshot \"${UBUNTU_SNAPSHOT_VERSION}\";" > /etc/apt/apt.conf.d/50snapshot \`
- **Problem:** the change promises in `docs/usage/core.md`, ADR 0022 and the Dockerfile comment that the image keeps the snapshot in apt's config, so `apt-get install` in a CI job and every child image's `apt-get update` use it. `images/core/smoke.sh` (and the child smoke scripts) never check this. If a later edit drops or renames `50snapshot`, or a child image or base swap overrides it, apt silently goes back to the live archive and every test still passes.
- **Suggested fix:** add a check to `images/core/smoke.sh`, for example that `apt-config dump APT::Snapshot` prints a non-empty value.

### Looked at and not raised
- **Regex manager:** the change from `[a-z-]` to `[a-z.-]` correctly matches `custom.ubuntu-snapshot`. The `versioning=regex:...` value has no whitespace, so the lazy capture works.
- **JSONata parsing:** the plain-format line filter, the `$match` groups, month lookup and day padding all produce `YYYYMMDDT000000Z` correctly for a real `Date:` line.
- **containerd.io pin:** `"containerd.io=${CONTAINERD_VERSION}~*"` with `extractVersion=^(?<version>[^~]+)~` and `versioning=deb` is consistent with how Docker names its package versions.
- **Release-wait rules:** `minimumReleaseAge: null` on the snapshot rule is fine, and the later `x.y.0` rule cannot match snapshot values.
- **Skipped TLS check on the first apt step:** the old code already fetched from the plain-HTTP archive, so this adds no new exposure. apt still checks signatures.
- **Plain-HTTP registry URL for the custom datasource:** an attacker on the network path could forge the `Date:` line. Whether that leads to anything harmful depends on how snapshot.ubuntu.com treats future timestamps, which the code doesn't show, so I'm leaving it as speculation.
- **Other Dockerfiles:** coder-template and devcontainer-base run no apt commands.

The ADR therefore states a false reason for one of the three, which is a small, non-blocking maintainability issue.

review.body:
The pinning design holds up. The containerd.io pin, the `--error-on=any` coverage, the host-scoped TLS skip and the regex-manager change all check out against the head commit.

One blocking issue: the Renovate `ubuntu-snapshot` datasource pins the snapshot to midnight of the day the security pocket last changed. That moment is before the publication that caused the bump, so the newest security fix is left out of the images until the pocket changes again on a later day. Details are inline.

There are also three non-blocking notes: no smoke test checks the snapshot pin, and two statements in ADR 0019 do not match what the Renovate config does.

comments.body:
**Bug (blocking): the proposed snapshot is taken before the security update that caused it.**

The template keeps only the day from the InRelease `Date:` line and appends `T000000Z`. A snapshot timestamp gives the archive as it was at that moment. The `Date:` line records when the pocket last changed, which is almost always after midnight, so the pinned snapshot does not include that change.

- **Trigger:** `resolute-security` is republished on 21 Nov 2026, and its InRelease reads `Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 14:07:12 UTC`. Nothing else lands in the pocket for a few days.
- **Path:** `renovate.json@customDatasources.ubuntu-snapshot.transformTemplates` produces `20261121T000000Z`. That value goes to `images/core/Dockerfile@ARG UBUNTU_SNAPSHOT_VERSION`, then into the `APT::Snapshot` line in `50snapshot`. Every `apt-get update` then reads the archive as it was at 00:00 on 21 Nov.
- **Outcome:** the 14:07 security fix is not in any image. Later lookups return the same `20261121T000000Z`, so Renovate proposes no further bump. The fix arrives only after the pocket changes on a later day, and that day's fix is again left out.

This breaks the guarantees in this datasource's `description` and in the ADR 0019 bullet ("bumps as soon as the archive changes, since it carries security fixes").

**Suggested fix:** also capture `(\d{2}):(\d{2}):(\d{2})` from the `Date:` line and build `YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ`. The `regex:` versioning on the Dockerfile pin already accepts any six-digit time. This drops the "at most one bump a day" property, so reword that in the description and in ADR 0022. If one bump a day has to stay, pin the next day's midnight instead.

**Tests (non-blocking): nothing checks that apt actually uses the snapshot.**

The main new behaviour is that apt in this image, its child images and CI jobs reads only the dated snapshot. `docs/usage/core.md` and ADR 0022 promise this. Neither `images/core/smoke.sh` nor the shared smoke library checks it. If `50snapshot` is dropped or renamed, or a base-image change turns snapshots off, the images go back to floating packages and CI stays green.

**Suggested fix:** in core's smoke test, check that `apt-config dump APT::Snapshot` prints `${UBUNTU_SNAPSHOT_VERSION}`, or at least a non-empty value.

**Docs (non-blocking): the shared reason is wrong for the new third kind.**

The lead-in says all three kinds skip the wait "because their registries do not say when a release was published". `renovate.json` exempts the Ubuntu snapshot for a different reason: `"minimumReleaseAge": null`, because it carries security fixes and has passed Ubuntu's -proposed testing. Only the Docker rule uses `timestamp-optional` for a registry without timestamps.

**Suggested fix:** shorten the lead-in to "Three kinds of pin skip the wait:" and give each bullet its own reason. The new bullet already has one.

**Docs (non-blocking): this claims more than the config does.**

The `ubuntu-snapshot` datasource reads only the `resolute-security` pocket's InRelease `Date:` and cuts it to the day. So the snapshot bumps when the security pocket changes, at most once a day, not whenever the archive changes; changes to `-updates`, for example, do not trigger a bump.

**Suggested fix:** "The Ubuntu archive snapshot bumps as soon as the security pocket changes, since it carries security fixes". Add the one-a-day limit only if the datasource keeps it; see the blocking comment on `renovate.json`.
